reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes BNB Miner/BNBChainMiner as a wallet-connected BNB staking or mining opportunity, directing viewers to join through a supplied link and connect a wallet. The presentation includes claims of a three percent payout, daily BNB earnings, and payments lasting over 400 days, alongside controls for hiring miners, compounding, and pocketing BNB.

citations.quote: i'm going to throw a thousand bucks i'm going to get this thing going
if you guys want to join after my link that'd be great
i'll be making three b and b per day

opening.argument: The speaker expressly qualifies the discussion as personal risk commentary rather than a promise: he says he is not a financial advisor, tells viewers to use only capital they are willing to lose, and acknowledges both possible gains and losses. That uncertainty matters because the presentation does not certify a safe or guaranteed outcome. The discussion is therefore better understood as conditional investment commentary accompanied by an explicit warning, not deceptive assurance.

citations.quote: Small risk capital guys, remember I'm not a financial advisor. I always put into this risk capital what you're willing to lose. You could make a lot, you could lose, but you never know guys.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes an invitation, a link, and an earnings estimate, but those excerpts do not establish a guarantee or conceal the risk qualification. The same presentation expressly says the viewer could lose and that the speaker is not a financial advisor. A promotional invitation can coexist with disclosed uncertainty; the cited material does not show that viewers were promised safety or certainty.

citations.quote: You could make a lot, you could lose, but you never know guys.
remember I'm not a financial advisor

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The disclaimer does not neutralize the concrete solicitation. The speaker says he will put in a thousand dollars, invites viewers to join through his link, and describes recurring daily BNB earnings. Saying losses are possible does not make a paid-return pitch ordinary commentary, especially when the presentation highlights compounding and income.

citations.quote: i'm going to throw a thousand bucks i'm going to get this thing going
if you guys want to join after my link that'd be great
i'll be making three b and b per day

opening.argument: The video can be read as an operational demonstration of how a crypto interface works. The speaker explicitly describes doing it live over the shoulder, then walks through connecting a wallet and using visible controls such as hiring miners, compounding, and pocketing BNB. The displayed account shows no miners and zero TVL at one point, so the material demonstrates interface flow rather than proving that a payout occurred. Its central useful content is procedural and explanatory.

citations.quote: what i'm going to do guys live over the shoulder

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the footage a demonstration does not change what is actually being demonstrated: a wallet-connected mining interface accompanied by earnings claims. The prosecution's point is not that a completed payout is shown, but that viewers are directed toward the operation. Still, the absence of a completed transaction supports the narrower reading that this is an interface walkthrough, not proof of a fraudulent outcome.

citations.quote: you just click on the connect the wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A tutorial format can still promote a scam mechanism. The walkthrough is paired with an invitation to join through the speaker's link and a stated plan to invest money, while the controls are specifically for miners, compounding, and withdrawing BNB. Showing the interface does not make the paid-return claims merely educational.

citations.quote: if you guys want to join after my link that'd be great
i'm going to throw a thousand bucks i'm going to get this thing going

opening.argument: The evidence supports, at most, promotion of an external crypto service, not proof of a scam mechanism. The interface shows buttons for hiring miners, compounding, and pocketing BNB, but the sampled screen also shows zero miners and zero TVL; no completed deposit, withdrawal, or payout is visible. The site's explanatory material describes community support, an algorithm, and estimated TVL, while expressly explaining that TVL is not a withdrawable lump sum. Those details are consistent with a service demonstration and leave the alleged transaction and outcome unestablished.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The link and wallet connection show promotion, but they do not by themselves prove a deposit, guaranteed return, downline payment, credential theft, or completed withdrawal. The prosecution treats interface labels and projected earnings as proof of mechanism, although the frames show only controls and account displays. On this record, the missing transaction evidence is material.

citations.quote: You could make a lot, you could lose, but you never know guys.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed withdrawal is unnecessary to identify the promoted mechanism. The speaker says he will put in money, directs viewers to join through his link, and describes three-percent and daily BNB earnings. The site's labels for hiring miners, compounding, and pocketing BNB show that this is not merely an ordinary retail service; the absence of a completed transaction does not cure the solicitation.
